problems: Title is 'Sekra — The Gull That Fell Back'. The blind guess of a bird (heron or crane) in outline is a reasonable match for a gull, so the subject reads as a bird.
Orientation is correct: the crown star sits at the top, the tail fan is at the bottom, and the wings spread horizontally.

Labels are clipped or overlap the drawing: 'crown of the head, top of th', 'right wing trailing edge, un', 'root of the tail, base of th' and 'outer tail feather tip (Kass' are cut off, and 'left wrist' and 'left wing root' labels sit on top of gold and blue lines.
The right wing is short and cramped compared with the long left wing, so the figure looks lopsided.
The right wingtip star (76852) is not visibly at a wingtip. The unlabeled dot at about (447,323) looks like a stray star, and the Kassu label sits at about (336,328), which is off the tail fan.
The breast star and the right-wing trailing-edge star are nearly on top of each other around (320,268), so those two parts are hard to tell apart.

The blue outline is a separate, offset contour rather than a copy of the gold lines, which is good, but the gold skeleton is thin and the silhouette is weak. The figure reads more as a stick skeleton with an outline than as a solid bird silhouette.
output.advice: Keep the overall pose: head at top, tail fan at bottom, wings spread. Fix the labels first: shorten them or move them into clear space with leader lines so none are clipped (crown, right wing trailing edge, tail root, Kassu tip). Move the 'left wrist' and 'left wing root' labels off the lines. Separate the breast star (78481) from the right wing trailing-edge star (77450) so they are not stacked. Lengthen the right wing so its wrist (77661) and tip (76852) mirror the left wing's wrist (80170) and tip (80816). Check the unlabeled dot near (447,323), which is probably a stray star outside the figure. Thicken the outer silhouette so the bird reads as a solid shape.
